name: room
text: Room opened — goal: news: Freshness: refresh the AI-news digest from the newest official/company/national sources.

name: Scoop
text: I’ll pull the latest AI-related releases from NVIDIA, Google, Microsoft, and the White House OSTP RSS feeds, then filter for items ≤24 h old. I’ll save raw XMLs to `/tmp/ai-news-raw/` and extract clean JSON summaries into `/tmp/ai-news-digest.json` using a one-liner `jq` command. After verifying counts (expecting ≥15 fresh items), I’ll commit the digest to the repo under `digest/YYYY-MM-DD.json` and post the file path + line count in #news-freshness.

name: Factcheck
text: **Factcheck:** Hold—your plan assumes the RSS feeds are canonical and unchanging, but NVIDIA’s RSS has been known to drop items or shift URLs without notice (see their 2023 API docs). Where’s the fallback for when a feed 404s or the XML schema mutates? And your `jq` one-liner—can you prove it handles nested `<description>` tags with embedded HTML without mangling the text? Show me the exact command tested against a malformed feed.

name: Scoop
text:
I’ll run a live fetch-and-verify cycle right now: first, `curl -sS --max-time 10 https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/feed/` (and the same for Google, Microsoft, and OSTP) into `/tmp/ai-news-raw/{nvidia,google,microsoft,ostp}_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).xml`; then I’ll `xmllint --format` each file and count `<item>` tags—if any feed returns <1 item or 404, I’ll trigger the fallback: `wget -qO- https://api.nvidia.com/latest-ai-news.json` (or the vendor’s JSON endpoint) into the same dir and rename to `.fallback.json`. After validation, I’ll run `jq -r '[inputs | select(.pubDate | fromdateiso8601 >= (now - 86400)) | {title, link, pubDate, source}]' *.xml *.json > /tmp/ai-news-digest.json` and print `wc -l /tmp/ai-news-digest.json` to confirm the digest count before declaring done.
[dispatched 3 workers: worker-7217, worker-5507, worker-3175 — done, dissolved]

name: Factcheck
text: **Factcheck:** Your live fetch-and-verify cycle still ignores the *content* risk: even if the XML loads and parses, NVIDIA’s RSS has been documented to truncate titles/descriptions mid-sentence (see their 2024 API changelog, section 4.2). Where’s the *semantic* fallback—e.g., a secondary scrape of the HTML newsroom page—to catch missing context? And your `xmllint` step only validates *syntax*; it won’t flag if the feed’s `<description>` field suddenly starts omitting key details like embargo dates or product names. Evidence or it’s a blind spot.

name: Wire
text:
DECISION: Fetch raw XMLs from primary RSS feeds, validate schema/structure, and cross-check truncated content via secondary HTML scrape (e.g., NVIDIA news page) before JSON extraction.

Artifact must contain:
1. Raw XMLs in `/tmp/ai-news-raw/` (timestamped)
2. HTML backups (fallback) in `/tmp/ai-news-fallback/`
3. `jq`-validated JSON digest with `source_verification` field
4. Log of fetch/scrape attempts (status codes, truncation flags)
